question: To obtain a Wisconsin school bus ("S") endorsement, a driver's vision must meet what minimum standard?
choice_a: 20/40 vision corrected or uncorrected in each eye, with at least 70 degrees field of vision in each eye
choice_b: 20/60 vision corrected in each eye only
choice_c: No specific vision standard, only a hearing standard
choice_d: 20/20 vision uncorrected in each eye
explanation: The manual requires at least 20/40 vision corrected or uncorrected in each eye, a minimum of 70 degrees field of vision in each eye, and the ability to identify traffic signal colors.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Wisconsin license requirements

question: What hearing standard must a school bus driver meet for the "S" endorsement?
choice_a: Hear a normal conversation at ten feet
choice_b: Hear a forced whisper at five feet, with or without a hearing aid
choice_c: Pass an audiometric test with no hearing aid allowed
choice_d: There is no hearing requirement for school bus drivers
explanation: The manual states drivers must be able to hear a forced whisper at five feet with or without a hearing aid.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Wisconsin license requirements

question: How often must a school bus driver pass a physical examination to retain the "S" endorsement?
choice_a: Every 5 years
choice_b: Only once, at initial licensing
choice_c: Every 2 years and upon renewal (every year if age 70 or older)
choice_d: Every 10 years
explanation: To retain the S endorsement, drivers must pass a physical every 2 years and upon renewal, and every year if age 70 or older.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Wisconsin license requirements

question: According to the manual, how often must school bus drivers age 70 or older be retested for the "S" endorsement?
choice_a: Only when they first turn 70
choice_b: Every 6 months
choice_c: Every 4 years
choice_d: Every 2 years
explanation: At each renewal of the S endorsement, or other time frames set by Wisconsin Statutes, school bus drivers must be retested; if 70 or older, they must be retested every 2 years.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Wisconsin license requirements

question: When must the doors of a school bus be kept closed while the bus is moving?
choice_a: Except when crossing railroad tracks
choice_b: Except during loading only
choice_c: Doors may be left open if traffic is light
choice_d: At all times, with no exceptions
explanation: General school bus rules require keeping doors closed when moving, except when crossing railroad tracks.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - General school bus rules

question: According to the general school bus rules, where should students with special needs be seated?
choice_a: In the back row, away from the driver
choice_b: Near the driver
choice_c: Wherever they choose to sit
choice_d: Standing near the front door
explanation: The rules direct drivers to seat students with special needs near the driver.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - General school bus rules

question: When should students be permitted to sit in the back row of seats on a school bus?
choice_a: Only on field trips
choice_b: Only students with special needs may sit there
choice_c: Only when the bus is filled
choice_d: Never, under any circumstances
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to keep children out of the back row of seats except when the bus is filled, since sitting near the front provides greater protection in rear-end collisions.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - General school bus rules

question: Under the general school bus rules, what must a driver NEVER do?
choice_a: Conduct a vehicle inspection before each trip
choice_b: Use approved pickup or discharge points
choice_c: Wear a safety belt
choice_d: Leave the bus unattended with the engine running and the keys in the ignition
explanation: The manual states a driver must NEVER leave the bus unattended with the engine running and the keys in the ignition.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - General school bus rules

question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: As much as 30 feet, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_b: 50 feet in all directions equally
choice_c: The danger zone only exists behind the bus
choice_d: 10 feet, with the first 5 feet being most dangerous
explanation: The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Danger zones

question: According to the manual, how far do the danger zones extend from the left and right sides and the rear bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet on each side and 5 feet behind
choice_b: 10 feet on each side and 10 feet behind
choice_c: 20 feet on each side and 20 feet behind
choice_d: There is no defined distance for the sides or rear
explanation: The danger zones extend 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Danger zones

question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because students always exit on the left
choice_b: Because the driver cannot open the door on that side
choice_c: Because of passing vehicles
choice_d: Because it is closest to the fuel tank
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing vehicles.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Danger zones

question: When properly adjusted, how far behind the bus should the outside mirrors allow the driver to see?
choice_a: 500 feet or 10 bus lengths
choice_b: 50 feet or 1 bus length
choice_c: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths
choice_d: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths
explanation: Mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Correct mirror adjustment

question: Where are the outside left and right side flat mirrors mounted on a school bus?
choice_a: At the left and right front corners of the bus at the side or front of the windshield
choice_b: Above the rear emergency door
choice_c: Inside the bus above the driver's head
choice_d: On the rear bumper
explanation: The outside flat mirrors are mounted at the left and right front corners of the bus at the side or front of the windshield.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Outside left and right side flat mirrors

question: How far can the blind spot behind a school bus extend, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only 10 feet
choice_b: 50 to 150 feet, and could extend up to 400 feet depending on bus length and width
choice_c: Exactly 1000 feet regardless of bus size
choice_d: There is no blind spot behind a school bus
explanation: The blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Outside left and right side flat mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located on a school bus?
choice_a: Inside the bus near the rear door
choice_b: On the roof of the bus
choice_c: Below the outside flat mirrors
choice_d: Above the outside flat mirrors
explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors and are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Outside left and right side convex mirrors

question: What is the primary purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors?
choice_a: To check tire pressure
choice_b: To monitor traffic 200 feet behind the bus
choice_c: To view passenger activity inside the bus
choice_d: To see the front bumper "danger zone" area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision, as well as the danger zones to the left and right.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Outside left and right side crossover mirrors

question: What is the primary purpose of the overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus?
choice_a: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_b: To check the front bumper danger zone
choice_c: To see 200 feet behind the bus
choice_d: To check tire clearance on turns
explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side and is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Overhead inside rearview mirror

question: When positioning the overhead inside rearview mirror, what should be visible at the top of the mirror?
choice_a: The bus's front bumper
choice_b: The top of the rear window
choice_c: The stop arm
choice_d: The service door only
explanation: The mirror should be positioned so the top of the rear window appears in the top of the mirror, and all students, including those right behind the driver, are visible.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.1 - Overhead inside rearview mirror

question: What kills more students each year than being killed as a passenger inside a school bus, according to the manual?
choice_a: High wind rollovers
choice_b: Fires on the bus
choice_c: Being struck while getting on or off the bus
choice_d: Railroad crossing incidents
explanation: The manual states more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Loading and unloading

question: May a school bus driver change the location of a bus stop on their own judgment?
choice_a: Yes, but only during winter weather
choice_b: Yes, if parents agree
choice_c: Yes, any time it seems safer
choice_d: No, never without written approval from the appropriate school district official
explanation: The manual states a driver should never change the location of a bus stop without written approval from the appropriate school district official.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Routes, stops, pickup and discharge points

topic: Flashing Red Lights and Stop Arm
question: How close may other vehicles legally stop to a school bus that has stopped and activated its flashing red warning lights?
choice_a: No closer than 20 feet
choice_b: No closer than 50 feet
choice_c: There is no minimum distance requirement
choice_d: No closer than 10 feet
explanation: All vehicles must stop no closer than 20 feet to a stopped school bus displaying flashing red warning lights, with an exception for vehicles traveling opposite on a divided highway.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Using flashing red warning lights

topic: Flashing Red Lights and Stop Arm
question: Under Wisconsin Statute s.346.48(1), which vehicles are NOT required to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red warning lights?
choice_a: Vehicles approaching from a side street
choice_b: Vehicles proceeding in the opposite direction on a divided highway
choice_c: All vehicles must stop regardless of direction or road type
choice_d: Vehicles following directly behind the bus
explanation: Operators of vehicles proceeding in the opposite direction on a divided highway are not required to stop for stopped school buses displaying flashing red warning lights per s.346.48(1), Wisconsin Statutes.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Using flashing red warning lights

topic: Flashing Red Lights and Stop Arm
question: When should flashing red warning lights NOT be used, according to the manual, unless required by local ordinance?
choice_a: On divided highways only
choice_b: In rural areas with no sidewalks
choice_c: Where both sides of the road have curb and sidewalk
choice_d: During daylight hours
explanation: The manual states not to use flashing red warning lights where both sides of the road have curb and sidewalk, unless required by local ordinance.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Using flashing red warning lights

question: In a 45 mph or greater speed zone, how far before stopping should a driver turn on the flashing amber warning lights?
choice_a: At least 500 feet before stopping
choice_b: Amber lights are not required in high-speed zones
choice_c: At least 100 feet before stopping
choice_d: At least 300 feet before stopping
explanation: In a 45 mph or greater speed zone, flashing amber warning lights should be turned on at least 300 feet before stopping.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Approaching the stop

question: In a speed zone of less than 45 mph, how far before stopping should the flashing amber warning lights be activated?
choice_a: At least 100 feet before stopping
choice_b: At least 300 feet before stopping
choice_c: At least 50 feet before stopping
choice_d: Immediately upon seeing a student at the stop
explanation: In a speed zone less than 45 mph, amber warning lights should be turned on at least 100 feet before stopping.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Approaching the stop

question: When bringing the bus to a full stop at a designated stop, how far away from students should the front bumper stop?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: At least 25 feet
choice_d: Exactly at the curb where students stand
explanation: The driver should bring the bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Approaching the stop

question: Under the Wisconsin exception in s.346.48(2)(c), when may school bus markings remain uncovered and flashing amber or red lights be used even outside normal route operation?
choice_a: Only when the bus is empty
choice_b: Never, markings must always be covered for non-school use
choice_c: If transporting children for any purpose
choice_d: Only during field trips approved by the state
explanation: The Wisconsin exception states that if transporting children for any purpose, school bus markings may remain uncovered and flashing amber or red lights used (s.346.48(2)(c)).
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Using flashing red warning lights

question: When loading or discharging students in areas where flashing warning lights are not required, how far before the stop should the yellow hazard lights be activated?
choice_a: At least 300 feet before the stop
choice_b: Hazard lights are not needed in this situation
choice_c: Only after the bus has fully stopped
choice_d: At least 100 feet before the stop
explanation: When flashing warning lights are not required, the driver should activate the yellow hazard lights at least 100 feet before the stop.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Without flashing warning lights

question: What should a driver do if unable to account for a student who was expected to board the bus at a stop?
choice_a: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_b: Honk the horn repeatedly and drive away
choice_c: Call the parents before doing anything else
choice_d: Leave and report it at the end of the route
explanation: If a driver cannot account for a student outside, the manual instructs to secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Loading procedures

question: How should students board the bus, according to the loading procedures?
choice_a: Quickly, in any order, to save time
choice_b: Slowly, in single file, using the handrail
choice_c: Two at a time to speed boarding
choice_d: In whatever order the driver signals individually
explanation: Students should board the bus slowly, in single file, and use the handrail; the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Loading procedures

question: What should a driver do with the ignition and parking brake if leaving the driver's compartment while loading at school?
choice_a: Nothing is required if the stop is brief
choice_b: Leave the engine running for climate control
choice_c: Turn off the ignition switch, remove the key, and set the parking brake
choice_d: Only set the parking brake; the key may stay in the ignition
explanation: When loading at school, if leaving the driver's compartment, the driver should turn off the ignition switch, remove the key, and set the parking brake.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Loading procedures at school

question: Where should students living on the left side of the road wait after exiting the bus, before crossing?
choice_a: Behind the bus, out of sight
choice_b: On the bus steps until signaled
choice_c: Immediately at the edge of the roadway
choice_d: 10 to 12 feet in front of the bus
explanation: Students living on the left side of the road should wait 10-12 feet in front of the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Unloading procedures on the route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, approximately how far from the side of the bus should they walk to a position where the driver can see them?
choice_a: 10 feet
choice_b: 20 feet
choice_c: They should not move away from the bus at all
choice_d: 5 feet
explanation: Students crossing the roadway should walk approximately 10 feet away from the side of the school bus to a position where the driver can see them.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Additional procedures for students who must cross the roadway

question: How far in front of the right corner of the bumper should a crossing student walk before stopping at the edge of the roadway?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: At least 25 feet
choice_d: Right at the bumper
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Additional procedures for students who must cross the roadway

question: May a school bus driver back the bus up while on school grounds during unloading?
choice_a: Only in an emergency
choice_b: Yes, if done slowly
choice_c: Never back a bus on school grounds
choice_d: Only with a spotter present
explanation: The unloading procedures at school explicitly state to never back a bus on school grounds.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Unloading procedures at school

question: After all students have exited at school, what should the driver do before leaving the unloading area?
choice_a: Only check the overhead mirror
choice_b: Nothing further is required
choice_c: Immediately drive away to stay on schedule
choice_d: Walk through the bus to check for hiding or sleeping students and items left behind
explanation: The driver should walk through the bus and check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students before preparing to leave.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Unloading procedures at school

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What should a student be told to do if they drop an object near the bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Leave the object, move to a point of safety, and attempt to get the driver's attention before retrieving it
choice_b: Ask another student to retrieve it for them
choice_c: Wait until the bus departs and retrieve it later
choice_d: Immediately retrieve it themselves
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, attempting to get the driver's attention before trying to retrieve the object.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Special dangers of loading and unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What safety hazard is described as "handrail hang-ups" in the manual?
choice_a: Students falling asleep in their seats
choice_b: Clothing, accessories, or body parts getting caught in the handrail or door while exiting
choice_c: Students losing grip on the handrail while boarding
choice_d: The handrail becoming loose or damaged
explanation: Students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or body parts got caught in the handrail or door as they exited the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Special dangers of loading and unloading

question: During a post-trip inspection, which item receives special attention because it is unique to school buses?
choice_a: Fuel gauge accuracy
choice_b: Tire tread depth
choice_c: Mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
choice_d: Engine oil level
explanation: The post-trip inspection should give special attention to items unique to school buses: mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Post-trip inspection

question: When using a power ramp to raise or lower a wheelchair, what does the manual instruct the driver to secure first?
choice_a: Neither needs securing on a power ramp
choice_b: Only the occupant's seatbelt
choice_c: The occupant, then the wheelchair
choice_d: The wheelchair, then the occupant
explanation: The manual states to secure the wheel (wheelchair) first and then the occupant.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.2 - Transporting persons with disabilities

question: What is described as the first and most important consideration when an emergency situation arises on a school bus?
choice_a: For the driver to recognize the hazard
choice_b: Evacuating all students immediately regardless of the situation
choice_c: Turning off the flashing warning lights
choice_d: Calling 911 immediately
explanation: The first and most important consideration is for the driver to recognize the hazard; if time permits, the driver should contact the dispatcher before deciding to evacuate.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Planning for emergencies

question: As a general rule, how is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis?
choice_a: By evacuating the bus immediately in every case
choice_b: By keeping students on the bus, unless doing so exposes them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_c: By having students exit through windows only
choice_d: By letting students decide individually whether to stay or leave
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Planning for emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition requiring a MANDATORY evacuation of the school bus?
choice_a: The heater is not working properly
choice_b: The bus is running 5 minutes behind schedule
choice_c: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_d: A student reports feeling carsick
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when it is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, among other mandatory conditions such as fire or imminent collision.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Determine need to evacuate bus

question: When conducting an evacuation drill on school grounds, which door should be used, according to the manual?
choice_a: The rear emergency door only
choice_b: Any door chosen at random each time
choice_c: The emergency roof hatch
choice_d: The front door only
explanation: The manual instructs using the school grounds to conduct an evacuation drill using the front door only; service door and emergency exit drills should be practiced in an area with no traffic.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: How far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic, should a safe evacuation place generally be located?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: At least 500 feet
choice_c: At least 25 feet
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: A safe place for students should be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep them from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, how far upwind of the bus should students be led?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: At least 300 feet
choice_c: At least 1,000 feet
choice_d: At least 50 feet
explanation: The manual states to lead students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and no building shelter is readily available, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Have students stand in a tight group beside the bus
choice_b: Keep all students on the bus with seatbelts fastened
choice_c: Escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert and have them lie face down with hands covering their heads
choice_d: Drive the bus away at maximum speed
explanation: If evacuation is ordered during a sighted tornado and no shelter is available, escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert, direct them to lie face down with hands covering their heads, far enough that the bus cannot topple on them, and avoid flash-flood areas.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: In a rear door evacuation, which students are directed to exit first?
choice_a: The youngest students first
choice_b: Students seated in the middle of the bus
choice_c: The driver, followed by all students at once
choice_d: Two patrol members or older children, who then help others out of the door
explanation: In the rear door evacuation procedure, two patrol members or older children are assigned to exit first and help the others out of the door.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: In a front door evacuation, which order do students follow when exiting?
choice_a: Left front seat first, then right front seat, alternating front to rear until all are off
choice_b: All students exit simultaneously regardless of seat
choice_c: Rear seats exit first, working toward the front
choice_d: Right front seat first, then left front seat, alternating front to rear
explanation: In the front door evacuation procedure, students in the left front seat exit first, followed by those in the right front seat, continuing to alternate from front to rear until all students are off.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: According to the manual, when should a student suspected of a neck or spinal injury be moved during an emergency?
choice_a: Immediately, to prevent further injury
choice_b: Only unless his or her life is in immediate danger
choice_c: Only after calling the parents for permission
choice_d: Students with such injuries should always be moved to the front door first
explanation: The manual instructs not to move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger, since special procedures are needed to prevent further injury.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Evacuation procedures

question: Following a crash or breakdown, what should the driver do to maximize the bus's visibility if it must remain in place?
choice_a: Have students stand outside near the road to flag traffic
choice_b: Turn off all lights to conserve the battery
choice_c: Move off the roadway if possible, activate hazard lights, and set out traffic warning devices
choice_d: Leave the bus exactly where it stopped with no lights
explanation: To maximize visibility after a crash or breakdown, the driver should move off the roadway if possible, activate hazard lights (and after dark, parking/clearance lights and strobe light if equipped), and set out traffic warning devices.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.3 - Handling emergencies

question: Under Wisconsin rules, must a school bus stop at railroad crossings even when it is empty?
choice_a: Only buses over a certain weight must stop
choice_b: Only buses without ABS must stop
choice_c: No, only loaded buses must stop
choice_d: Yes, all school buses, loaded or empty, must stop unless the tracks are posted "exempt" or "abandoned"
explanation: In Wisconsin, all school buses, loaded or empty, must stop at railroad crossings unless the tracks are posted exempt or abandoned.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Railroad-highway crossings

question: At a passive railroad crossing (no traffic control device), who is responsible for deciding whether it is safe to proceed?
choice_a: The decision rests entirely with the driver
choice_b: The school district transportation office
choice_c: The railroad company
choice_d: A designated student lookout
explanation: At passive crossings, the decision to proceed rests entirely in the driver's hands after recognizing the crossing, searching for a train, and deciding if there is sufficient clear space.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Types of crossings

question: What does an active railroad-highway crossing have that a passive crossing does not?
choice_a: A round yellow advance warning sign
choice_b: A traffic control device, such as flashing red lights, with or without bells and gates
choice_c: Pavement markings with an "X" and "RR"
choice_d: A crossbuck sign
explanation: Active crossings have a traffic control device installed, which can include flashing red lights with or without bells, and flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Types of crossings

question: What must a driver do when approaching the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Ignore it since it only applies to trucks
choice_b: Immediately stop regardless of a train's presence
choice_c: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming
choice_d: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
explanation: The advance warning sign tells the driver to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Warning signs and devices

question: Where must the front of the school bus remain if there is a white stop line painted on the pavement before railroad tracks?
choice_a: At least 100 feet past the stop line
choice_b: The stop line does not apply to school buses
choice_c: Even with the crossbuck sign
choice_d: Behind the white stop line while stopped at the crossing
explanation: There may be a white stop line painted on the pavement before the railroad tracks, and the front of the school bus must remain behind this line while stopped at the crossing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Warning signs and devices

question: If there is no white line painted on the pavement, where must the bus stop relative to a crossbuck sign?
choice_a: The bus must stop before the crossbuck sign
choice_b: The bus may stop anywhere within 200 feet of the sign
choice_c: The bus should stop after passing the crossbuck sign
choice_d: Crossbuck signs do not require a stop
explanation: If there is no white line painted on the pavement, the driver must stop the bus before the crossbuck sign.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Warning signs and devices

question: What should a driver do if the gate stays down after a train has already passed?
choice_a: Carefully drive around the gate
choice_b: Do not drive around the gate; instead, contact your dispatcher
choice_c: Break through the gate immediately
choice_d: Wait exactly five minutes then proceed regardless
explanation: If the gate stays down after the train passes, the driver should not drive around the gate but instead contact the dispatcher.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Warning signs and devices

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, approximately how far before the crossing should the driver activate yellow hazard lights?
choice_a: Only after coming to a complete stop
choice_b: 1,000 feet before the crossing
choice_c: Approximately 200 feet, but at least 100 feet before the crossing
choice_d: Exactly 50 feet before the crossing
explanation: The driver should activate yellow hazard lights approximately 200 feet, but at least 100 feet, before the crossing to make intentions known.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Recommended procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, the bus should stop in the farthest right driving lane no closer than 15 feet and no farther than how many feet from the nearest rail?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: The bus should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where the driver has the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Recommended procedures

question: While stopped at a railroad crossing, what should the driver do besides opening the service door and driver's window?
choice_a: Turn off all radios and noisy equipment and silence the passengers
choice_b: Have all students move to the left side of the bus
choice_c: Rev the engine to warn any approaching train
choice_d: Turn on the radio to listen for train alerts
explanation: At the crossing, the driver should press and hold the service brakes, turn off all radios and noisy equipment, silence the passengers, and completely open the service door and driver's window to look and listen for an approaching train.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Recommended procedures

question: When crossing the tracks, in what gear should the bus cross, and what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: A high gear; avoid using the brakes
choice_b: A low gear; do not change gears while crossing
choice_c: Neutral, coasting across; avoid braking
choice_d: Any gear is fine as long as speed is under 10 mph
explanation: The driver should cross the tracks in a low gear and must not change gears while crossing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Recommended procedures

question: Until what point must the service door remain open when crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: The service door does not need to be opened at railroad crossings
choice_b: Until the rear wheels have cleared the last set of tracks
choice_c: Until the front wheels of the bus have cleared the first set of tracks for each required stop
choice_d: The door may be closed as soon as the bus begins moving
explanation: The service door shall remain open until the front wheels of the bus have cleared the first set of tracks for each required stop, and shall be closed before shifting.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Recommended procedures

question: If a bus stalls or becomes trapped on railroad tracks, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Stay on the bus and wait for help
choice_b: Move everyone to the rear of the bus and wait
choice_c: Attempt to restart the bus for at least two minutes before evacuating
choice_d: Get everyone out of the bus and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle both away from the tracks and toward the train
explanation: If the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, everyone must get out and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Special situations

question: As a general rule for containment or storage areas at railroad crossings, how many feet should be added to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable containment area?
choice_a: 15 feet
choice_b: 30 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 5 feet
explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area at a crossing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.4 - Special situations

question: When should a driver deal with an on-bus behavior problem that arises during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Immediately, even while students are still boarding or exiting
choice_b: Wait until the students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away, or pull the bus over if necessary
choice_c: Never; loading and unloading behavior problems should be ignored
choice_d: Only after completing the entire route
explanation: During loading and unloading, the driver's full concentration is required; if there is a behavior problem, the driver should wait until students unloading are safely off and away, or pull the bus over to handle the problem.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.5 - Don't deal with on-bus problems when loading and unloading

question: Where may a driver put a student off the bus for disciplinary reasons?
choice_a: Anywhere the parent requests by phone
choice_b: At any convenient location along the route
choice_c: Only at school or at his or her designated school bus stop
choice_d: At the nearest police station
explanation: The manual states never to put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.5 - Handling serious problems

question: Who develops the rules for student behavior on school buses?
choice_a: The Wisconsin Department of Transportation exclusively
choice_b: The bus manufacturer
choice_c: Individual bus drivers, independently
choice_d: Local school boards
explanation: Local school boards develop the rules for student behavior, and copies should be distributed to students and their parents.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.5 - Handling serious problems

question: Air brake vehicles, including buses, are required to have Antilock Braking Systems (ABS) if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1999
choice_c: January 1, 2000
choice_d: October 1, 1998
explanation: The Department of Transportation requires ABS on air brake vehicles, including trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies, built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.6 - Vehicles required to have ABS

question: In an emergency braking situation on a bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Steering around obstacles
choice_b: Pumping the brakes
choice_c: Applying the brakes at all
choice_d: Shifting to a lower gear
explanation: In emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS; instead, use only the braking force necessary and brake as they always would.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.6 - Braking with ABS

question: What does the manual say ABS will NOT do?
choice_a: Come into play when a wheel would normally lock up from over-braking
choice_b: Help the driver avoid wheel lock-up on slippery surfaces
choice_c: Necessarily shorten stopping distance, and will not compensate for bad brakes or poor maintenance
choice_d: Assist with steering around an obstacle while braking
explanation: The manual lists several safety reminders, including that ABS will not necessarily shorten stopping distance and will not compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.6 - Safety reminders

question: The flashing white strobe light on a school bus is required equipment on buses initially registered on or after what date?
choice_a: January 1, 2000
choice_b: It has always been required on all school buses
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: October 1, 1998
explanation: The strobe light is required equipment on buses initially registered on or after October 1, 1998, and optional on buses registered before that date.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.7 - Strobe lights

question: The manual compares the side of a school bus in strong winds to what object?
choice_a: A sail on a sailboat
choice_b: An anchor
choice_c: A parachute
choice_d: A brick wall
explanation: The manual states the side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and strong winds can push the bus sideways or even tip it over in extreme conditions.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.7 - Driving in high winds

question: When backing a school bus is unavoidable and a lookout is posted, where should the lookout be positioned and what is their role?
choice_a: Outside the bus, giving hand signals to guide the driver
choice_b: Preferably inside the bus looking out the rear window, to warn of obstacles, but not to give directions on how to back
choice_c: In front of the bus, walking backward ahead of it
choice_d: On the bus roof, using a radio
explanation: The lookout should preferably be posted inside the school bus looking out the rear window to warn about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, but should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.7 - Backing

question: May a school bus be backed when students are outside the bus?
choice_a: Only during dismissal at school
choice_b: Yes, as long as hazard lights are on
choice_c: Never; a school bus should never be backed when students are outside the bus
choice_d: Yes, if the driver honks the horn first
explanation: The manual states you should never back a school bus when students are outside the bus, since backing is dangerous and increases the risk of collision.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.7 - Backing

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have, according to the manual?
choice_a: Up to six feet
choice_b: School buses have no tail swing
choice_c: Up to one foot
choice_d: Up to three feet
explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so drivers need to check mirrors before and during turning movements to monitor it.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10.7 - Tail swing

question: Between what dates are studded snow tires allowed on school buses in Wisconsin, per s.347.45(2)(c)2, Wisconsin Statutes?
choice_a: November 15 to April 1
choice_b: December 1 to February 28
choice_c: Studded snow tires are never allowed on school buses
choice_d: October 1 to March 1
explanation: The manual notes that studded snow tires are allowed on school buses between November 15th and April 1st, per s.347.45(2)(c)2, Wisconsin Statutes.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Vehicle inspection for school bus

question: What role does the vehicle inspection play in the examination for an original or renewal school bus ("S") endorsement?
choice_a: It is optional and not evaluated
choice_b: The driver will be evaluated on the inspection of the vehicle as part of the examination
choice_c: Only a mechanic may perform the inspection for the exam
choice_d: It is only required for the original endorsement, never for renewal
explanation: The manual states the driver will be evaluated on the inspection of the vehicle as part of the examination for an original or renewal school bus endorsement.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 10 - Vehicle inspection for school bus
